shared.category: B.1 Assumed concepts — Ordinary English
shared.text: Contemporary general-purpose English in its ordinary, nontechnical senses

shared.category: B.1 Assumed concepts — Ordinary English
shared.text: The baseline does not admit a specialized sense merely because the term uses a familiar word.

shared.category: B.1 Assumed concepts — Ordinary English
shared.text: For example, *lease*, *control*, *model*, and *significance* still require admission as domain terms.

shared.category: B.2 Assumed notation — Included
shared.text: Arithmetic: `+ − × /` and parentheses.

shared.category: B.2 Assumed notation — Included
shared.text: Equality and comparison: `=`, `≠`, `<`, `≤`, `>`, and `≥`.

shared.category: B.2 Assumed notation — Included
shared.text: Percent `%` and plain ratios such as `3:1`.

shared.category: B.2 Assumed notation — Included
shared.text: Plain numeric ranges such as `1–5`.

shared.category: B.2 Assumed notation — Included
shared.text: The following notation is not in the baseline. Writers define the notation at first use, even when the notation looks standard.

shared.category: B.2 Assumed notation — Included
shared.text: Variables, named constants, function application, and subscripted indexing

shared.category: B.2 Assumed notation — Included
shared.text: Approximation `≈`, powers, absolute value, scientific notation, and interval notation such as `[0, 1]`

shared.category: B.2 Assumed notation — Included
shared.text: Summation `Σ`, product `Π`, logarithms, exponentials, factorial, and Big-O notation

shared.category: B.2 Assumed notation — Included
shared.text: Set notation, including membership, subsets, unions, intersections, and set-builder notation

shared.category: B.2 Assumed notation — Included

shared.category: B.2 Assumed notation — Included

shared.category: B.2 Assumed notation — Included

shared.category: B.2 Assumed notation — Included
shared.text: `argmax` / `argmin`, `∝`, `∀` / `∃`, and Greek letters carrying conventional meanings (θ for parameters, α for rates).

shared.category: B.3 Explicitly not assumed
shared.text: The writer shall not use these concepts without admitting them through the §2.3 ladder. Familiarity is not knowledge (§0.3.2).

shared.category: B.3 Explicitly not assumed — Role and education
shared.text: The baseline does not assume a computer science education or a software engineering job title.

shared.category: B.3 Explicitly not assumed — Role and education
shared.text: The baseline does not assume professional coding experience or the depth of a seasoned software engineer.

shared.category: B.3 Explicitly not assumed — Programming implementation
shared.text: Admit programming-language syntax and implementation concepts not listed in §B.1.

shared.category: B.3 Explicitly not assumed — Programming implementation
shared.text: Admit data structures and algorithms beyond ordinary lists and tables.

shared.category: B.3 Explicitly not assumed — Programming implementation
shared.text: Complexity analysis, Big-O notation, divide and conquer, dynamic programming, and intractability remain unassumed.

shared.category: B.3 Explicitly not assumed — Systems and data infrastructure
shared.text: Admit threads, concurrency, race conditions, memory hierarchy, caching, compilation, and floating-point behavior.

shared.category: B.3 Explicitly not assumed — Systems and data infrastructure
shared.text: Admit CPU/GPU execution models, file-system internals, timeouts, retries, load balancing, and scaling models.

shared.category: B.3 Explicitly not assumed — Systems and data infrastructure
shared.text: Eventual consistency, database schemas, indexes, transactions, joins, key-value stores, and SQL behavior remain unassumed.

shared.category: B.3 Explicitly not assumed — Domain and organization-specific concepts
shared.text: Admit specialized reliability, platform, security, governance, legal, financial, scientific, or product terms unless §B.1 lists the intended sense.

shared.category: B.3 Explicitly not assumed — Community and process shorthand
shared.text: Examples that remain unassumed include venue prestige as evidence, "SOTA," "camera-ready," "rebuttal," "SEV-1," "five whys," "two-person rule," and unexplained status labels or approval gates.

design-rfc.text: The reader recognizes a proposal organized around context, requirements, a proposed design, alternatives, risks, rollout, and unresolved questions.

decision-record.text: The reader recognizes a compact record of status, context, decision, and consequences. The reader expects an explicit recorded decision.

procedure.text: The reader recognizes prerequisites, ordered steps, verification, recovery, and escalation as instruction-document conventions.

explanation.text: The reader recognizes a concept-to-mechanism explanation supported by examples and bounded by limits.

incident.text: The reader recognizes impact and timeline as factual records. The reader treats causal analysis as a separate interpretation. The reader treats remediation and follow-up as separate jobs.

technical-report.text: The reader recognizes a report that separates system or method, evidence, interpretation, limitations, and reproducibility or verification.

research-paper.text: The reader recognizes navigation derived from introduction, methods, results, and discussion (IMRaD). The reader treats citations as source pointers and distinguishes results from discussion.

investigation-log.text: The reader recognizes dated, append-only entries that separate objective, configuration or context, observations, interpretation, and next step.

epic.text: The reader recognizes a concise product requirements document organized around one strategic outcome, scope, success measures, technical invariants, child tasks, and completion.

task.text: The reader recognizes one tactical outcome with classification, one user journey or engineering-only outcome, paths, completion conditions, integrated acceptance, and child subtasks.

subtask.text: The reader recognizes one non-independent contribution linked to one parent task and one named parent completion condition.

maintenance-comment.text: The reader recognizes one comment change set with its change scope, repeated comment records, and boundaries.
